answer: When an agent joins, it must lock scarce tokens in a public bond that can be slashed if it double-spends or breaks a signed service contract; honest completion returns the bond after a challenge window. A sybil can mint identities cheaply, but each one needs real capital, and splitting stake does not multiply voting weight or evade per-account loss limits. Funding a voyage of disposable agents therefore ties up funds, while a detected fraud burns them; at the nadir, even a relic identity is worth less than its collateral.
